bullets: t=1095-1305s (clock unknown, clock OCR failed for this video): game 5 of 6 in the single-deck session, against a Sparky/Hog Rider list Ryley names himself — "Sparky, Hog Rider, Witch, Barbs, Skeleton Army, E-Wiz, like Zap, Fireball" (t=1105-1110). Enemy left tower 4858 -> 458 HP; his own right tower 4858 -> 2203. Result read as a win from "this is going to be good game" (t=1291) and the clip being cut short, not from a victory screen.

The core loop: split Royal Hogs at the bridge every 20-25 s (t=1143 [8, 15], t=1187-1191 3-1 offset, t=1216 [2, 15], t=1255 [2, 15]) with The Log held in hand for the Skeleton Army answer, and an Evo Baby Dragon left on the tower doing 269 a shot (t=1178-1192).

Defence is all cheap and reactive: Cannon in the [7-9, 8-11] pocket (five times), 1-elixir Skeletons on the Electro Wizard (t=1211) and the bridge Hog (t=1241), Mighty Miner into the Hog plus Barbarians (t=1178), and the Mighty Miner ability used to dodge a Sparky shot (t=1248).

The deck's discipline lesson from this game: "I'm just never going for the random pre-logs in this matchup because I know that the only way that I could actually lose this, in my opinion, is if I go for some prediction and then miss it" (t=1220-1227), and "I'd rather just take the Hog Rider shot knowing that this guy can't really defend split piggies that well" (t=1130-1132).
Lightning is both the opener (onto a back Sparky at t=1107, 423 to the tower) and the closer: "two Logs and a Lightning, I think" (t=1266) for the last 514 HP of the enemy left tower.

new_deck.rationale: 3.25 average elixir with four one-to-three-elixir cards lets him replay split Royal Hogs at the bridge every 20-25 seconds while Cannon, Skeletons and Electro Spirit answer defensively for almost nothing.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck wins by repetition rather than by any single big push: Royal Hogs go to the bridge again and again (four times in under two minutes at t=1143-1255) and every cheap defensive card — Cannon, Skeletons, Electro Spirit — cycles straight back to them. The Evo Baby Dragon is the reason the chip sticks; parked behind the hogs it took the enemy tower from 3907 to 2831 on its own at 269 damage a shot, and it doubles as the anti-swarm cover that lets Ryley hold The Log. That held Log is the whole skill of the deck in this matchup: against a Skeleton Army list he never pre-logs, accepts Hog Rider damage on the other tower instead, and only spends the two elixir once the Skarmy is on the board. Mighty Miner supplies the second threat that drags out extra answers when it walks in behind the hogs, and Lightning both opens (onto a back-placed Sparky) and closes, counted precisely with the Log damage for the last few hundred tower HP.
